narration_lines: Rain lands on soil, grass, roofs and roads. Each landing is the start of a different journey.
Soil is like a sponge. It drinks the rain.
A sponge can fill up. Soil that is full of water is called saturated soil. When rain comes faster than full soil can take it in, water stays on top.
Extra water flows across the ground. This flowing water is called runoff. It slides to lower places.
In towns, water slips into drains under the street.
Drains lead to canals. Canals lead to rivers. Rivers carry water to the sea.
Some water waits in puddles and leaves. The sun lifts it back up as vapour. This is evaporation.
People also catch rain. Tanks, ponds and reservoirs keep it for dry days.
Every drop of rain takes one of these journeys. Water that is stored can journey again another day.
Our paper boats follow the water downhill. Next time it rains, watch where the water goes!
